items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: They shall be nameless, but like so now I get this phone call, and I said well, I’ll tell you what to do, call John Levy and tell John to get ahold of Jimmy Jones and the bass player, Sproles.

ctx.x: Well when they catch you up there on a narcotics charge, then you’re not allowed back in, that’s all. Two of the guys had been through that. They shall be nameless, but like so now I get this phone call, and I said well, I’ll tell you what to do, call John Levy and tell John to get ahold of Jimmy Jones and the bass player, Sproles.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: when Milt was too busy I would get Clarke Terry.

ctx.x: Yeah. He's got it. It's built in him, you know? And he's so well rounded as a musician, I don't think you're going to find many any better than Milt, or as good. Because he's -- in fact, when I was beginning to write, back east, Milt was my contractor. I used to split it with Milt, when Milt was too busy I would get Clarke Terry.
